text:
Jordan: quick heads-up — perf alert from canary: small chat reqs (<=64 tokens) are seeing ~2.4ms host-side p50 increase after the recent tokenization changes. digging now but wanted to flag.

Priya: ack. is that measured on grpc ingress or http?

Jordan: grpc ingress. stack: nginx -> grpc-proxy -> host-preproc. profile shows hotspots in request parsing and a new memcpy in token framing.

Ken: can you paste the flame? small messages are usually dominated by header decode + writev.

Jordan: pasted below (trimmed):

```
grpc_proxy::handle_frame  35%  (header parse + metadata)
host_preproc::tokenize   28%  (new split code path)
socket::writev           18%  (many tiny buffers)
kv_cache::lookup         7%
other                    12%
```

Priya: looks like two issues: extra copy in tokenize split, and fragmented writev from framing. both hit tiny reqs badly.

Marta: infra-bot reports increased packet count on the path, likely due to non-coalesced streaming chunks.

infra-bot: [deploy-monitor] Canary: ingress-packet-rate +14% on region-us-west-2 for service=host-preproc (since 1798999800).

Ken: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) switch tokenization path to zero-copy span for ascii runs, 2) add a writev coalescer before socket writes, 3) debounce tiny streaming chunks for <=64 token responses. any of those low-risk?

Priya: zero-copy span: low-risk if we keep fallback. writev coalescer: medium risk but can be taught to only run for small responses. debounce streaming chunks: risky for streaming UX but we can make it opt-in via route header.

Jordan: test results from local patch stack: zero-copy reduced tokenize time from 0.9ms -> 0.2ms for tiny requests. coalescer reduced socket syscalls by ~60% and net p50 improved by ~1.1ms. combined gives ~1.5ms reduction.

Marta: any KV cache effects? small requests often hit very cold KV entries and that adds jitter.

Jordan: KV hit rate unchanged in canary. but the new token split increases key churn for prefix-based cache keys (we split tokens earlier, key becomes shorter -> more insertions).

Ken: maybe normalize cache key to full original text for tiny requests to avoid churn. or only insert into KV for responses > 128 tokens.

Priya: agree on threshold insert. also add a simple switch to prefer lower-latency kernels for short sequences: our kernel selector currently leans on throughput-estimates, we should bias for latency when seq_len <= 64.

Jordan: opened PR with three changes: zero-copy token span, writev coalescer with small-window heuristic, and kv-insert-threshold=128. link: https://git.redwood/infra/host-preproc/pulls/412

Ken: I'll take the kernel selector tweak in a follow-up — need perf tests to avoid hurting large-batch throughput.

Priya: can we add a canary config to make debounce streaming chunks route-scoped and opt-out for dev? so users using SSE/streaming still get immediate chunks.

Jordan: yeah added route option in the PR description. deploying canary now to us-west-2 with 5% traffic. will report back after 30m.

Marta: thanks — set an alert for packet-rate and p50. if anything spikes revert the coalescer first. :thumbsup:
